parole.significato: alphabet (an ordered set of letters used in a language)
parole.testo: From Late Latin alphabētum, from Ancient Greek ἀλφάβητος (alphábētos), from ἄλφα (álpha) and βῆτα (bêta), the first two letters of the Greek alphabet, from Phoenician and Classical Hebrew aleph (ox) and beth (house), so called because their shape resembled or represented these objects.
From Late Latin basaltes, a misspelling of Latin basanites, from Ancient Greek βασανίτης (basanítēs), from βάσανος (básanos, “touchstone”), from Egyptian bḫn (“a hard stone”) b-x:n-O39
Borrowed from Late Latin colophōn, from Ancient Greek κολοφών (kolophṓn, “peak or finishing touch”).
From Late Latin paradigma, from Ancient Greek παράδειγμα (parádeigma).

parole.testo: Borrowed from Late Latin trāchīa (“windpipe, trachea”), from Ancient Greek τρᾱχεῖᾰ (trākheîă, “rough, rugged”), the substantivized feminine of τρᾱχῠ́ς (trākhŭ́s, “rough, rugged”), and an ellipsis of τρᾱχεῖᾰ ᾰ̓ρτηρῐ́ᾱ (trākheîă ărtērĭ́ā, “rough artery, windpipe”). The adjective is from Proto-Hellenic
